title.zh: 卷87 節義:于什門 段進 石文德 汲固 王玄威 婁提 劉渴侯
title.en: Volume 87: Morality and Righteousness - Yu Shenmen, Duan Jin, Shi Wende, Ji Gu, Wang Xuanwei, Lou Ti, Liu Kehou
title.raw: 卷87 節義:于什門 段進 石文德 汲固 王玄威 婁提 劉渴侯 Volume 87: Morality and Righteousness - Yu Shenmen, Duan Jin, Shi Wende, Ji Gu, Wang Xuanwei, Lou Ti, Liu Kehou

sentences.zh: 于什門 段進 石文德 汲固 王玄威 婁提 劉渴侯 朱長生 于提 馬八龍 門文愛 晁清 劉侯仁 石祖興 邵洪哲 王榮世 胡小虎 孫道登 李几 張安祖 王閭

translations.literal: Yu Shenmen, Duan Jin, Shi Wende, Ji Gu, Wang Xuanwei, Lou Ti, Liu Kehou, Zhu Changsheng, Yu Ti, Ma Balong, Men Wen'ai, Chao Qing, Liu Hourén, Shi Zuxing, Shao Hongzhe, Wang Rongshi, Hu Xiaohu, Sun Daodeng, Li Ji, Zhang Anzu, and Wang Lü.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shenmen, Duan Jin, Shi Wende, Ji Gu, Wang Xuanwei, Lou Ti, Liu Kehou, Zhu Changsheng, Yu Ti, Ma Balong, Men Wen'ai, Chao Qing, Liu Hourén, Shi Zuxing, Shao Hongzhe, Wang Rongshi, Hu Xiaohu, Sun Daodeng, Li Ji, Zhang Anzu, and Wang Lü.

sentences.zh: 大義重於至聞自日人。

translations.literal: Great righteousness outweighs the utmost renown; since antiquity among people. [The first nine characters of this line are corrupt in the manuscript and cannot be fully reconstructed.]
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity, people have held that great righteousness outweighs the highest fame—the opening line of our text is damaged beyond recovery in the received version.

sentences.zh: [2]慕之者蓋希，行之者實寡。

translations.literal: Those who admire it are perhaps few; those who actually practice it are truly rare.
translations.idiomatic: Many may admire such conduct, but few truly practice it.

sentences.zh: 至於輕生蹈節，臨難如歸，殺身成仁，死而無悔，自非耿介苦心之人，鬱怏激氣之士，亦何能若斯。

translations.literal: As for lightly valuing life yet treading in integrity, facing peril as though returning home, sacrificing the body to accomplish humanity and dying without regret—unless one were a sternly upright man of tormented heart, a man of pent resentment and rising spirit, how could one achieve such as this?
translations.idiomatic: To hold life lightly yet honor duty, to meet danger as if going home, to give one's body for humane virtue and die without regret—only a man of unyielding integrity, nursing deep resolve and burning spirit, could act thus.

sentences.zh: 僉列之傳，名節義云。

translations.literal: Collectively we array their biographies; their fame is integrity and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Here we gather their lives together under the rubric of righteous fidelity.

sentences.zh: 于簡，字什門，代人也。

translations.literal: Yu Jian, courtesy name Shenmen, was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jian, styled Shenmen, came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 太宗時為謁者，使喻馮跋。

translations.literal: In the reign of Emperor Taizong he served as Herald and was sent to instruct Feng Ba.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Taizong he served as Herald and was dispatched to deliver the imperial message to Feng Ba.

sentences.zh: 及至和龍，住外舍不入，使人謂跋曰：「大魏皇帝有詔，須馮主出受，然後敢入。

translations.literal: When he reached Helong, he lodged in an outer quarter and would not enter, sending someone to tell Feng Ba: "The Great Wei emperor has an edict; I must wait until Lord Feng comes out to receive it before I dare enter."
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Helong he stayed in an outer lodge and refused to enter, sending word to Feng Ba: "The Great Wei emperor has issued an edict. Lord Feng must come out to receive it; only then will I dare enter."

sentences.zh: 」跋使人牽逼令入，見跋不拜，跋令人按其項。

translations.literal: " Feng Ba sent men to drag and force him in; he saw Feng Ba but did not bow, and Feng Ba had someone press down on his neck.
translations.idiomatic: " Feng Ba had men drag him in by force. He faced Feng Ba but would not bow, so Feng Ba ordered someone to press his head down.

sentences.zh: 什門曰：「馮主拜受詔，吾自以賓主致敬，何須苦見逼也！

translations.literal: Shenmen said: "When Lord Feng bows to receive the edict, I myself shall pay respect as between guest and host—why must you torment me so!"
translations.idiomatic: Shenmen said, "When Lord Feng bows to receive the edict, I shall pay respect as between guest and host. Why torment me like this?"

sentences.zh: 」與跋往復，聲氣厲然，初不撓屈。

translations.literal: " He and Feng Ba went back and forth; his voice was stern and forceful, and from the first he did not yield.
translations.idiomatic: " He and Feng Ba argued back and forth, his voice fierce and unwavering; he never bent from the start.

sentences.zh: 既而跋止什門。

translations.literal: Presently Feng Ba detained Shenmen.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Feng Ba held Shenmen captive.

sentences.zh: 什門於羣眾之中，回身背跋，被袴後襠以辱之。

translations.literal: Amid the crowd Shenmen turned his back to Feng Ba, dropped his trousers and exposed his rear to insult him.
translations.idiomatic: Before the assembled crowd Shenmen turned his back on Feng Ba, dropped his trousers, and bared his rear to shame him.

sentences.zh: 既見拘留，隨身衣裳敗壞略盡，蟣虱被體。

translations.literal: Once detained, the clothes on his person were worn out nearly entirely, and lice swarmed over his body.
translations.idiomatic: Once held prisoner, his clothes were worn to rags and lice covered his body.

sentences.zh: 跋遺以衣服，什門拒而不受。

translations.literal: Feng Ba sent him clothes, but Shenmen refused and would not accept them.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ba offered him clothes, but Shenmen refused them.

sentences.zh: 和龍人皆歎曰：「雖古烈士，無以過也！

translations.literal: The people of Helong all sighed: "Even the martyrs of antiquity could not surpass this!"
translations.idiomatic: The people of Helong all marveled: "Even the heroes of old could not equal this!"

sentences.zh: 」歷二十四年，[3]後馮文通上表稱臣，乃送什門歸。

translations.literal: " After twenty-four years, later Feng Wentong submitted a memorial declaring himself a subject, and only then was Shenmen sent back.
translations.idiomatic: " He remained there twenty-four years; only after Feng Wentong submitted a memorial acknowledging subjection was Shenmen sent home.

sentences.zh: 拜治書侍御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Attendant Censor of the Imperial Library.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Attendant Censor of the Imperial Library.

sentences.zh: 世祖下詔曰：「什門奉使和龍，值狂豎肆虐，勇志壯厲，不為屈節，雖昔蘇武何以加之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu issued an edict: "Shenmen on mission to Helong encountered a mad villain rampaging; his courage and resolve were mighty and fierce and he would not compromise his integrity—even the Su Wu of old could not surpass him."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu issued an edict: "Shenmen served as envoy at Helong when a violent usurper ran riot. His courage was fierce and he would not bend his integrity—even Su Wu of old could hardly surpass him."

sentences.zh: 」賜羊千口、帛千匹，進為上大夫，策告宗廟，頒示天下，咸使聞也。

translations.literal: " He was granted a thousand sheep and a thousand bolts of silk, promoted to Grand Master of the First Order, with proclamation at the ancestral temple and circulation throughout the realm so all might hear.
translations.idiomatic: " He received a thousand sheep and a thousand bolts of silk, was promoted to Grand Master of the First Order, and the court reported his deed to the ancestral temple and proclaimed it throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 段進，不知何許人也。

translations.literal: Duan Jin—his native place is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Jin was a man of unknown origin.

sentences.zh: 世祖初，為白道守將。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shizu's reign he was garrison commander of Baidao.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Shizu's reign he served as garrison commander at Baidao.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕大檀入塞，圍之，力屈被執。

translations.literal: The Rouran ruler Datan entered the frontier, besieged him, and when his strength was spent he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran khan Datan raided across the border, besieged the post, and when resistance failed Duan was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 進抗聲大罵，遂為賊殺。

translations.literal: Jin shouted back in a loud voice and reviled them, and the bandits therefore killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Duan shouted his defiance and cursed them until the enemy slew him.

sentences.zh: 世祖愍之，追贈安北將軍，賜爵顯美侯，諡曰莊。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu pitied him and posthumously enfeoffed him as General Who Pacifies the North, granting the title Marquis of Xianmei, with the posthumous name Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu mourned him and posthumously made him General Who Pacifies the North, with the title Marquis of Xianmei and the posthumous name Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 石文德，河中蒲坂人也，[4]有行義。

translations.literal: Shi Wende was a man of Puban in Hedong, noted for righteous conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Wende came from Puban in Hedong and was known for his integrity.

sentences.zh: 真君初，縣令黃宣在任喪亡，宣單貧無期親，文德祖父苗以家財殯葬，持服三年，奉養宣妻二十餘載。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhenjun era the magistrate Huang Xuan died in office; Xuan was alone and poor with no close kin, and Wende's grandfather Miao used family wealth for the burial, wore mourning three years, and supported Xuan's wife for more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenjun era the county magistrate Huang Xuan died in office. Xuan was poor and without kin, so Wende's grandfather Miao buried him at family expense, observed three years of mourning, and supported Xuan's wife for more than twenty years.

sentences.zh: 及亡，又衰絰斂祔，率禮無闕。

translations.literal: When she died, he again wore hemp mourning, laid her out, and joined her spirit tablet to the husband's—all rites observed without omission.
translations.idiomatic: When she died in turn, he again wore full mourning, laid her out, and enshrined her beside her husband, observing every rite without lapse.

sentences.zh: 自苗逮文德，刺史守令卒官者，制服送之。

translations.literal: From Miao down to Wende, whenever a provincial inspector, prefect, or magistrate died in office, they wore mourning and escorted the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: From Miao through Wende, whenever a provincial inspector, prefect, or magistrate died in office, the family wore mourning and saw the funeral through.

sentences.zh: 五世同居，閨門雍睦。

translations.literal: Five generations dwelt together; within the household all was harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Five generations lived under one roof, and the household was harmonious throughout.

sentences.zh: 又梁州上言天水白石縣人趙令安、孟蘭彊等，四世同居，行著州里。

translations.literal: Moreover Liang Province reported that Zhao Ling'an, Meng Lanqiang, and others of Baishi County in Tianshui had dwelt together four generations, their conduct renowned in the district.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Province also reported that Zhao Ling'an, Meng Lanqiang, and others of Baishi County in Tianshui had lived together four generations, their virtue known throughout the region.

sentences.zh: 詔並標牓門閭。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that plaques be posted at their gates and lanes.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered commemorative plaques posted at all their gates.

sentences.zh: 汲固，東郡梁城人也。

translations.literal: Ji Gu was a man of Liangcheng in Dong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Gu came from Liangcheng in Dong Commandery.

sentences.zh: 為兗州從事。

translations.literal: He served as Registrar of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Registrar of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 刺史李式坐事被收，吏民皆送至河上。

translations.literal: The provincial inspector Li Shi was arrested for an offense, and officials and commoners all escorted him to the river.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial Inspector Li Shi was arrested for an offense, and officials and commoners escorted him as far as the river.

sentences.zh: 時式子憲生始滿月，式大言於眾曰：「程嬰、杵臼何如人也！

translations.literal: At the time Shi's son Xian had just reached one month of age; Shi spoke loudly before the crowd: "What sort of men were Cheng Ying and Gongsun Chujiu!"
translations.idiomatic: Shi's infant son Xian was only a month old. Shi cried out to the crowd, "What manner of men were Cheng Ying and Gongsun Chujiu!"

sentences.zh: 」固曰：「今古豈殊。

translations.literal: " Gu said: "Past and present—how are they different?"
translations.idiomatic: " Ji Gu replied, "Past and present are not so different."

sentences.zh: 」遂便潛還，不復回顧，徑來入城，於式婦閨抱憲歸藏之。

translations.literal: " He then slipped back secretly without turning his head again, went straight into the city, entered the women's quarters of Shi's wife, took Xian in his arms, and returned to hide him.
translations.idiomatic: " He slipped away without a backward glance, went straight into the city, entered Shi's wife's inner quarters, took the infant Xian, and hid him away.

sentences.zh: 及捕者收憲屬，有一婢產男，母以婢兒授之。

translations.literal: When the arresting officers came to seize Xian's household, a maid had just borne a son; the mother gave them the maid's child instead.
translations.idiomatic: When officers came to seize the boy, a maid had just given birth; Shi's wife handed over the maid's infant in his place.

sentences.zh: 事尋泄，固乃攜憲逃遁，遇赦始歸。

translations.literal: The matter was soon exposed; Gu then fled with Xian, and only when an amnesty was declared did he return.
translations.idiomatic: The ruse was soon discovered, and Ji fled with Xian until an amnesty allowed them to return.

sentences.zh: 憲即為固長育至十餘歲，恒呼固夫婦為郎婆。

translations.literal: Xian was thereafter raised by Gu to more than ten years of age and always called Gu and his wife "Father and Mother."
translations.idiomatic: Ji raised Xian to his teens, and the boy always addressed Ji and his wife as Father and Mother.

sentences.zh: 後高祐為兗州刺史，嘉固節義，以為主簿。

translations.literal: Later Gao You became Inspector of Yan Province, admired Gu's integrity and righteousness, and appointed him Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Gao You became Inspector of Yan Province, he admired Ji's fidelity and made him Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 王玄威，恒農北陝人也。

translations.literal: Wang Xuanwei was a man of Beishan in Hengnong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuanwei came from Beishan in Hengnong.

sentences.zh: 顯祖崩，玄威立草廬於州城門外，衰裳蔬粥，哭踴無時。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzu died, Xuanwei erected a thatched hut outside the provincial city gate, wore hemp mourning and ate vegetables and gruel, and wept and stamped without regard to time.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzu died, Xuanwei built a thatched hut outside the provincial capital, wore hemp mourning, lived on vegetables and gruel, and wept and stamped at all hours.

sentences.zh: 刺史苟頹以事表聞。

translations.literal: The provincial inspector Gou Tui memorialized the matter to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial Inspector Gou Tui reported the matter to court.

sentences.zh: 詔令問狀，玄威稱：「先帝統御萬國，慈澤被於蒼生，含氣之類莫不仰賴，玄威不勝悲慕，中心知此，不知禮式。

translations.literal: An edict ordered inquiry into his circumstances; Xuanwei stated: "The late emperor ruled the myriad realms; his merciful grace covered the living masses—all breathing creatures looked up to him. Xuanwei cannot bear his grief and longing; in my heart I know this, but I do not know the forms of ritual."
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered an inquiry. Xuanwei said, "The late emperor ruled the realm; his mercy embraced all living things, and every creature under heaven relied on him. I cannot contain my grief; I feel it in my heart, though I do not know the proper forms of mourning."

sentences.zh: 」詔問玄威欲有所訴，聽為表列。

translations.literal: " The edict asked whether Xuanwei wished to present any petition and permitted him to set it forth in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: " The edict asked whether he wished to submit a petition and allowed him to do so in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 玄威云：「聞諱悲號，竊謂臣子同例，無所求謁。

translations.literal: Xuanwei said: "On hearing the tabooed name I wail in grief; I take it that subject and son are alike in this—I have nothing to request or petition for."
translations.idiomatic: Xuanwei replied, "Hearing the late emperor's name I weep aloud. I believe all subjects share this grief and have nothing to ask of the throne."

sentences.zh: 」及至百日，乃自竭家財，設四百人齋會。

translations.literal: " When the hundredth day arrived, he exhausted his family wealth to hold a vegetarian feast for four hundred people.
translations.idiomatic: " On the hundredth day he spent his entire family fortune to host a vegetarian feast for four hundred people.

sentences.zh: 忌日，又設百僧供。

translations.literal: On the anniversary of death he again provided offerings for a hundred monks.
translations.idiomatic: On the anniversary he again provided offerings for a hundred monks.

sentences.zh: 至大除日，詔送白紬袴褶一具，與玄威釋服，下州令表異焉。

translations.literal: When the day of full removal of mourning came, an edict sent one set of white silk trousers and jacket, had Xuanwei lay aside mourning, and ordered the province to record his exceptional conduct.
translations.idiomatic: When the period of mourning ended, the court sent a set of white silk garments so Xuanwei could leave mourning, and ordered the province to note his exceptional conduct.

sentences.zh: 婁提，代人也。

translations.literal: Lou Ti was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Ti came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 顯祖時為內三郎。

translations.literal: In the reign of Emperor Xianzu he served as Inner Third-Rank Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xianzu he served as an Inner Third-Rank Guard.

sentences.zh: 顯祖暴崩，提謂人曰：「聖主升遐，安用活為！

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzu died suddenly, Ti said to others: "The sage lord has ascended on high—what use is living!"
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzu died suddenly, Lou said to those around him, "The sage lord has departed—what use is life?"

sentences.zh: 」遂引佩刀自刺，幾至於死。

translations.literal: " He then drew his belt dagger and stabbed himself, nearly dying.
translations.idiomatic: " He drew his belt dagger and stabbed himself, nearly dying.

sentences.zh: 文明太后詔賜帛二百匹。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming issued an edict granting two hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming ordered two hundred bolts of silk bestowed on him.

sentences.zh: 時有敕勒部人蛭拔寅兄地于，坐盜食官馬，依制命死。

translations.literal: At the time there were two men of the Chile tribe, Zhibayin and his elder brother Diyu; for stealing and eating government horses they were sentenced to death by regulation.
translations.idiomatic: At that time two Chile tribesmen, Zhibayin and his elder brother Diyu, were sentenced to death for stealing government horses.

sentences.zh: 拔寅自誣己殺，兄又云實非弟殺，兄弟爭死，辭不能定。

translations.literal: Bayin falsely accused himself of the killing; the elder brother also said his younger brother had not in fact done it—the brothers vied to die, and their statements could not be settled.
translations.idiomatic: Bayin confessed to the crime himself, while his brother insisted the younger man was innocent; the two brothers competed to accept death, and the court could not decide between their accounts.

sentences.zh: 高祖詔原之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu issued an edict pardoning them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu pardoned them both by edict.

sentences.zh: 劉渴侯，不知何許人也。

translations.literal: Liu Kehou—his native place is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kehou was a man of unknown origin.

sentences.zh: 禀性剛烈。

translations.literal: His inborn nature was fierce and unyielding.
translations.idiomatic: He was fierce and unyielding by nature.

sentences.zh: 太和中，為徐州後軍，以力死戰，眾寡不敵，遂禽。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era he served as Rear Army of Xuzhou, fought to the death with all his strength, was outnumbered, and was captured.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe era he served in the rear guard at Xuzhou, fought to the death, was overwhelmed by superior numbers, and was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 瞋目大罵，終不降屈，為賊所殺。

translations.literal: He glared and reviled loudly, never submitting in the end, and the bandits killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He glared and cursed them until the enemy slew him, never yielding to the end.

sentences.zh: 高祖贈立忠將軍、平州刺史、上庸侯，賜絹千匹、穀千斛。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu posthumously enfeoffed him as General Who Establishes Loyalty, Governor of Ping Province, and Marquis of Shangyong, granting a thousand bolts of silk and a thousand hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu posthumously made him General Who Establishes Loyalty, Governor of Ping Province, and Marquis of Shangyong, with a thousand bolts of silk and a thousand hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 有嚴季者，亦為軍校尉，與渴侯同殿，勢窮被執，終不降屈，後得逃還。

translations.literal: There was one Yan Ji, also a military company commander; he fought in the same engagement as Kehou, was captured when strength was spent, never submitted in the end, and later escaped and returned.
translations.idiomatic: A company commander named Yan Ji fought in the same battle; when defeat was certain he too was captured but never yielded, and later escaped back to Wei territory.

sentences.zh: 除立節將軍，賜爵五等男。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Establishes Integrity and granted the fifth-rank noble title of Baron.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General Who Establishes Integrity and ennobled as a fifth-rank baron.

sentences.zh: 朱長生及于提，並代人也。

translations.literal: Zhu Changsheng and Yu Ti were both men of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Changsheng and Yu Ti both came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 高祖時，以長生為員外散騎常侍，與提俱使高車。

translations.literal: In the reign of Emperor Gaozu, Changsheng was made Extraordinary Attendant Cavalier in Regular Attendance and, together with Ti, was sent on mission to the Gaoche.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Gaozu, Changsheng was appointed Extraordinary Attendant Cavalier and sent with Ti as envoys to the Gaoche.

sentences.zh: 至其庭，高車主阿伏至羅責長生等拜，長生拒之曰：「我天子使，安肯拜下土諸侯！

translations.literal: On reaching their court, the Gaoche ruler Avuzhiluo demanded that Changsheng and the others bow; Changsheng refused, saying: "I am an envoy of the Son of Heaven—how could I bow to a borderland lord!"
translations.idiomatic: At the Gaoche court their ruler Avuzhiluo demanded that the envoys bow. Changsheng refused: "I am the Son of Heaven's envoy—how could I bow to a frontier chieftain?"

sentences.zh: 」阿伏至羅乃不以禮待。

translations.literal: " Avuzhiluo thereupon did not treat them according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: " Avuzhiluo then treated them without proper ceremony.

sentences.zh: 長生以金銀寶器奉之，至羅既受獻，長生曰：「為臣內附，宜盡臣禮，何得口云再拜而實不拜！

translations.literal: Changsheng presented gold, silver, and precious vessels to him; once Avuzhiluo had accepted the tribute, Changsheng said: "As a subject who has submitted inwardly, you ought to perform the full rites of a subject—how can you say you will bow twice yet in fact not bow!"
translations.idiomatic: Changsheng presented gold, silver, and precious vessels as tribute. Once Avuzhiluo had accepted them, Changsheng said, "You have submitted as a subject—perform the full rites of submission. How can you promise to bow twice and then not bow at all?"

sentences.zh: 」呼出帳，命眾中拜。

translations.literal: " He called him out of the tent and ordered him to bow before the assembled multitude.
translations.idiomatic: " He summoned Avuzhiluo from the tent and ordered him to bow before the assembled crowd.

sentences.zh: 阿伏至羅慚其臣下，大怒曰：「帳中何不教我拜，而辱我於大眾！

translations.literal: " Avuzhiluo was shamed before his subjects and said in great anger: "Why did you not teach me to bow inside the tent, yet humiliate me before the great crowd!"
translations.idiomatic: " Avuzhiluo, shamed before his followers, raged: "Why did you not tell me to bow in private, yet humiliate me before the whole assembly!"

sentences.zh: 」奪長生等獻物，囚之叢石之中，兵脅之曰：「汝能為我臣則活，如其不降，殺汝！

translations.literal: " He seized the gifts Changsheng and the others had presented, imprisoned them among the rocky hills, and soldiers threatened them, saying: "If you can become my subjects you will live; if you do not submit, you will be killed!"
translations.idiomatic: " He seized their gifts, imprisoned them in the stony hills, and soldiers threatened them: "Become my subjects and live; refuse and die!"

sentences.zh: 」長生與于提瞋目厲聲責之曰：「豈有天子使人拜汝夷，我寧為魏鬼，不為汝臣！

translations.literal: " Changsheng and Ti glared and rebuked him in stern voices: "How could an envoy of the Son of Heaven bow to you barbarians! I would rather be a ghost of Wei than your subject!"
translations.idiomatic: " Changsheng and Ti glared and shouted their rebuke: "How could the Son of Heaven's envoy bow to you barbarians! I would rather be a ghost of Wei than your subject!"

sentences.zh: 」至羅彌怒，絕其飲食。

translations.literal: " Avuzhiluo grew still angrier and cut off their food and drink.
translations.idiomatic: " Avuzhiluo flew into a greater rage and cut off their food and drink.

sentences.zh: 從行者三十人皆降，至羅乃給以肉酪，惟長生與提不從，乃各分徙之。

translations.literal: The thirty who had accompanied them all submitted; Avuzhiluo then gave them meat and curds, but only Changsheng and Ti would not comply, so he had them separately exiled.
translations.idiomatic: All thirty of their attendants submitted; Avuzhiluo gave them meat and curds, but Changsheng and Ti alone refused, so he had them exiled to separate places.

sentences.zh: 積三歲，乃得還。

translations.literal: After three years they were at last able to return.
translations.idiomatic: After three years they were finally able to return.

sentences.zh: 高祖以長生等守節遠同蘇武，甚嘉之，拜長生河內太守，于提隴西太守，並賜爵五等男。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu, because Changsheng and the others had kept their integrity and were far comparable to Su Wu, greatly commended them, appointing Changsheng Governor of Henei and Ti Governor of Longxi, and granting both the fifth-rank title of Baron.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu praised them for holding their integrity in a manner rivaling Su Wu of old, appointed Changsheng Governor of Henei and Ti Governor of Longxi, and ennobled both as fifth-rank barons.

sentences.zh: 從者皆為令長。

translations.literal: Those who had accompanied them were all made magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: Their attendants were all appointed district magistrates.

sentences.zh: 馬八龍，武邑武強人也。

translations.literal: Ma Balong was a man of Wuqiang in Wuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Balong came from Wuqiang in Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 輕財重義。

translations.literal: He held wealth lightly and valued righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He held wealth lightly and prized righteousness.

sentences.zh: 友人武遂縣尹靈哲在軍喪亡，八龍聞即奔赴，負屍而歸，以家財殯葬，為制緦服。

translations.literal: His friend Yin Lingzhe of Wusui County died on campaign; on hearing of it Balong rushed at once to the scene, carried the corpse back on his shoulders, buried him at family expense, and wore the hemp mourning of the closest kin.
translations.idiomatic: When his friend Yin Lingzhe of Wusui County died on campaign, Balong rushed to the field, carried the body home on his back, buried him at his own expense, and wore the full mourning of a close kinsman.

sentences.zh: 撫其孤遺，恩如所生。

translations.literal: He nurtured the orphan left behind with affection as though the child were his own.
translations.idiomatic: He raised the orphan left behind with the love of a father.

sentences.zh: 州郡表列，詔表門閭。

translations.literal: The province and commandery memorialized his case, and an edict ordered a plaque posted at his gate and lane.
translations.idiomatic: The province reported his conduct, and the court ordered a commemorative plaque at his gate.

sentences.zh: 門文愛，汲郡山陽人也。

translations.literal: Men Wen'ai was a man of Shanyang in Ji Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Men Wen'ai came from Shanyang in Ji Commandery.

sentences.zh: 早孤，供養伯父母以孝謹聞。

translations.literal: Orphaned early, he supported his uncle and aunt and was known for filial care and diligence.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he supported his uncle and aunt and was renowned for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 伯父亡，服未終，伯母又亡。

translations.literal: When his uncle died, before mourning was complete his aunt also died.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle died, and before that mourning was finished his aunt died as well.

sentences.zh: 文愛居喪，持服六年，哀毀骨立。

translations.literal: Wen'ai observed mourning, wearing the garments six years; his grief wasted him until only bone remained.
translations.idiomatic: Wen'ai mourned six years in all, his grief so severe that he was wasted to bone.

sentences.zh: 鄉人魏中賢等相與標其孝義。

translations.literal: His fellow townsmen Wei Zhongxian and others together commended his filial righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: His neighbors Wei Zhongxian and others jointly commended his filial conduct.

sentences.zh: 晁清，遼東人也。

translations.literal: Chao Qing was a man of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Chao Qing came from Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 祖暉，濟州刺史、潁川公。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hui was Governor of Ji Province and Duke of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Hui had been Governor of Ji Province and Duke of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 清襲祖爵，例降為伯。

translations.literal: Qing inherited his grandfather's enfeoffment, which by regulation was reduced to Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Qing inherited his grandfather's title, which by regulation was reduced to marquis.

sentences.zh: 為梁城戍將。

translations.literal: He served as garrison commander of Liangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He served as garrison commander at Liangcheng.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍攻圍，糧盡城陷，清抗節不屈，為賊所殺。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan besieged the city; when provisions were exhausted the city fell; Qing resisted with integrity and would not submit, and the bandits killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Yan besieged the city and supplies ran out, Liangcheng fell; Qing held firm and refused to yield, and the enemy killed him.

sentences.zh: 世宗褒美，贈樂陵太守，諡曰忠。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong praised him, posthumously enfeoffing him as Governor of Leling, with the posthumous name Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong commended him and posthumously made him Governor of Leling, with the posthumous name Loyal.

sentences.zh: 子榮賓襲。

translations.literal: His son Rongbin inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rongbin inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 劉侯仁，豫州人也。

translations.literal: Liu Hourén was a man of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hourén came from Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 城人白早生殺刺史司馬悅，據城南叛。

translations.literal: A townsman, Bai Zaosheng, killed the provincial inspector Sima Yue, seized the southern part of the city, and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: A local man named Bai Zaosheng killed Provincial Inspector Sima Yue, seized the southern quarter of the city, and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 悅息朏，走投侯仁。

translations.literal: Yue's son Fei fled in distress to Hourén.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's son Fei fled to Hourén for protection.

sentences.zh: 賊雖重加購募，又嚴其捶撻，侯仁終無漏泄，朏遂免禍。

translations.literal: Although the bandits repeatedly increased the reward for his capture and also beat him severely, Hourén never divulged the secret, and Fei thus escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Though the rebels raised the bounty on his head and beat him savagely, Hourén never revealed Fei's hiding place, and the boy was spared.

sentences.zh: 事寧，有司奏其操行，請免府籍，敍一小縣，詔可。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, the relevant offices memorialized his conduct, requesting removal from the prefectural register and appointment to a small county; the edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: After order was restored, officials reported his conduct and asked that he be struck from the prefectural rolls and given a small county post; the court approved.

sentences.zh: 石祖興，常山九門人也。

translations.literal: Shi Zuxing was a man of Jiumen in Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zuxing came from Jiumen in Changshan.

sentences.zh: 太守田文彪、縣令和真等喪亡，祖興自出家絹二百餘匹，營護喪事。

translations.literal: When the prefect Tian Wenbiao, the magistrate He Zhen, and others died, Zuxing contributed more than two hundred bolts of silk from his household to arrange and oversee their funerals.
translations.idiomatic: When Prefect Tian Wenbiao, Magistrate He Zhen, and others died, Zuxing supplied more than two hundred bolts of silk from his own household to manage their funerals.

sentences.zh: 州郡表列，高祖嘉之，賜爵二級，為上造。

translations.literal: The province and commandery memorialized his case; Emperor Gaozu commended him, granted two ranks of nobility, and made him Shangzao.
translations.idiomatic: The province reported his deeds; Emperor Gaozu praised him, raised his noble rank by two steps, and enfeoffed him as Shangzao.

sentences.zh: 後拜寧陵令，卒。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Magistrate of Ningling and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed magistrate of Ningling and died in office.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書李韶奏其節義，請加贈諡，以奬來者，靈太后令如所奏。

translations.literal: Li Shao, Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, memorialized his integrity and righteousness, requesting an added posthumous title to encourage those who come after; Empress Dowager Lingming ordered as memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shao, Minister of Personnel, praised his fidelity and asked for a posthumous title to encourage others; Empress Dowager Lingming approved.

sentences.zh: 有司諡曰恭。

translations.literal: The relevant offices gave the posthumous name Gong.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted him the posthumous name Respectful.

sentences.zh: 邵洪哲，上谷沮陽人也。

translations.literal: Shao Hongzhe was a man of Juyang in Shanggu.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Hongzhe came from Juyang in Shanggu.

sentences.zh: 縣令范道榮先自朐城歸款以除縣令，[5]道榮鄉人徐孔明，妄經公府，訟道榮非勳，道榮坐除名。

translations.literal: The magistrate Fan Daorong had earlier submitted from Qucheng in allegiance and was thereby removed as magistrate;[5] Daorong's fellow townsman Xu Kongming falsely appealed to the public offices, suing that Daorong had no merit, and Daorong was dismissed and struck from the register.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Fan Daorong had earlier surrendered from Qucheng and been appointed magistrate;[5] a townsman named Xu Kongming falsely petitioned the authorities that Daorong had no merit, and Daorong was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 羇旅孤貧，不能自理。

translations.literal: A wanderer, alone and poor, he could not manage for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Destitute and alone in a strange place, he could not fend for himself.

sentences.zh: 洪哲不勝義憤，遂代道榮詣京師，明申曲直。

translations.literal: Hongzhe, unable to bear his righteous indignation, thereupon went to the capital on Daorong's behalf and clearly set forth right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhe, overcome by righteous anger, went to the capital on Daorong's behalf and laid out the full truth of the case.

sentences.zh: 經歷寒暑，不憚劬勞，道榮卒得復雪。

translations.literal: Passing through cold and heat, he did not shrink from toil, and Daorong at last had his name cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Through winter and summer he labored without complaint until Daorong's name was cleared.

sentences.zh: 又北鎮反亂，道榮孤單，無所歸附。

translations.literal: When the Northern Garrison rebelled again, Daorong was isolated with nowhere to turn.
translations.idiomatic: When the Northern Garrison rose in revolt, Daorong was left alone with nowhere to go.

sentences.zh: 洪哲兄伯川復率鄉人來相迎接，送達幽州。

translations.literal: Hongzhe's elder brother Bochuan again led fellow townsmen to meet and escort him, delivering him to You Province.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhe's elder brother Bochuan again led townsfolk to fetch him and escorted him safely to You Province.

sentences.zh: 道榮感其誠節，訴省申聞。

translations.literal: Daorong was moved by their sincere integrity and appealed to the provincial authorities to report it.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by their loyalty, Daorong petitioned the provincial authorities to report their conduct.

sentences.zh: 詔下州郡，標其里閭。

translations.literal: An edict went down to the provinces and commanderies ordering a plaque at their lane and hamlet.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered plaques posted at their gates throughout the province.

sentences.zh: 王榮世，陽平館陶人也。

translations.literal: Wang Rongshi was a man of Guantao in Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rongshi came from Guantao in Yangping.

sentences.zh: 為三城戍主、方城縣子。

translations.literal: He served as garrison commander of Sancheng and Viscount of Fangcheng County.
translations.idiomatic: He was garrison commander of Sancheng and Viscount of Fangcheng.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍攻圍，力窮知不可全，乃先焚府庫，後殺妻妾。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan besieged the city; when strength was spent and he knew it could not be preserved, he first burned the government storehouses, then killed his wife and concubines.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Yan besieged the city and resistance failed, knowing the post could not be saved, he burned the government stores and then killed his wife and concubines.

sentences.zh: 及賊陷城，與戍副鄧元興等俱以不屈被害。

translations.literal: When the bandits took the city, he and the deputy garrison commander Deng Yuanxing and others were all killed for refusing to submit.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, he and Deputy Commander Deng Yuanxing and others were killed for refusing to yield.

sentences.zh: 肅宗下詔褒美忠節，進榮世爵為伯，贈齊州刺史；

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong issued an edict praising their loyal integrity, promoting Rongshi's enfeoffment to Earl and posthumously enfeoffing him as Governor of Qi Province;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong commended their loyalty, promoted Rongshi's title to earl, and posthumously made him Governor of Qi Province;

sentences.zh: 元興開國子，贈洛州刺史。

translations.literal: Yuanxing was made Founding Viscount and posthumously enfeoffed as Governor of Luo Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxing was made Founding Viscount and posthumously appointed Governor of Luo Province.

sentences.zh: 胡小虎，河南河陰人也。

translations.literal: Hu Xiaohu was a man of Heyin in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Xiaohu came from Heyin in Henan.

sentences.zh: 少有武氣。

translations.literal: In youth he had a martial spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a youth he had a warrior's spirit.

sentences.zh: 正光末，為統軍於晉壽。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhenguang era he served as Army Commander at Jinshou.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Zhenguang era he served as army commander at Jinshou.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，蕭衍將樊文熾等寇邊，益州刺史邴虬遣長史和安固守小劍，文熾圍之。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era Xiao Yan's general Fan Wenchì and others raided the frontier; the Governor of Yi Province Bing Qiu sent his Chief Clerk He An to hold Xiaojian firmly, and Wenchì besieged it.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiaochang era, Liang generals led by Fan Wenchì raided the border. Yi Province Governor Bing Qiu sent Chief Clerk He An to hold Xiaojian, and Wenchì besieged the fortress.

sentences.zh: 虬命小虎與統軍崔珍寶同往防拒。

translations.literal: Qiu ordered Xiaohu and Army Commander Cui Zhenbao to go together to defend against them.
translations.idiomatic: Bing ordered Xiaohu and Army Commander Cui Zhenbao to reinforce the defense together.

sentences.zh: 文熾掩襲小虎、珍寶，並擒之。

translations.literal: Wenchì launched a surprise attack on Xiaohu and Zhenbao and captured them both.
translations.idiomatic: Wenchì ambushed them and took both Xiaohu and Zhenbao prisoner.

sentences.zh: 文熾攻小劍未陷，乃將珍寶至城下，使謂和安曰：「南軍強盛，北救不來，豈若歸款，取其富貴。

translations.literal: Wenchì had not yet taken Xiaojian; he then brought Zhenbao to the foot of the wall and had him tell He An: "The southern army is strong; northern relief will not come—would it not be better to submit and gain wealth and honor?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiaojian had not yet fallen. Wenchì brought Zhenbao to the wall and had him call to He An: "The southern army is strong and northern relief will not come. Why not surrender and win wealth and rank?"

sentences.zh: 」和安命射之，乃退。

translations.literal: " He An ordered archers to shoot at him, and they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " He An ordered his archers to shoot, and the enemy withdrew.

sentences.zh: 復逼小虎與和安交言，小虎乃慷慨謂安曰：「我柵不防，為賊所虜。

translations.literal: They again forced Xiaohu to speak with He An; Xiaohu then said passionately to An: "My stockade was not defended and I was captured by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: They forced Xiaohu to speak with He An again. Xiaohu cried out to him, "Our stockade was poorly defended and I was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 觀其兵士，勢不足言，努力堅守。

translations.literal: Looking at their soldiers, their strength is not worth mentioning—strive to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: Look at their troops—their strength is nothing. Hold the fortress with all your might.

sentences.zh: 魏行臺傳梁州遣將已至。

translations.literal: The Wei Mobile Headquarters reports that Liang Province has sent generals who have already arrived.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei field headquarters reports that reinforcements from Liang Province have already arrived.

sentences.zh: 」[6]賊以刀毆擊，言不得終，遂害之。

translations.literal: "[6] The bandits struck him with blades; he could not finish speaking, and they killed him.
translations.idiomatic: "[6] The enemy beat him with blades before he could finish, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 三軍無不歎其壯節，哀其死亡。

translations.literal: Throughout the three armies none failed to admire his stalwart integrity and mourn his death.
translations.idiomatic: The whole army marveled at his courage and mourned his death.

sentences.zh: 賊尋奔敗，禽其次將蕭世澄、陳文緒等一十一人。

translations.literal: The bandits soon fled in defeat, and eleven of their officers including the deputy general Xiao Shicheng and Chen Wenxu were captured.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy soon fled in defeat, and eleven officers including deputy commanders Xiao Shicheng and Chen Wenxu were taken.

sentences.zh: 行臺魏子建壯其氣概，啟以世澄購其屍柩，乃獲骸骨歸葬。

translations.literal: Mobile Headquarters Wei Zijian admired his spirit, memorialized that Shicheng be used to ransom his coffin, and thus obtained his remains for burial at home.
translations.idiomatic: Field headquarters chief Wei Zijian admired his spirit, petitioned to exchange the captive Xiao Shicheng for his body, and brought his remains home for burial.

sentences.zh: 孫道登，彭城呂縣人也。

translations.literal: Sun Daodeng was a man of Lü County in Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Daodeng came from Lü County in Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 永安初，為蕭衍將韋休等所虜，面縛臨刃，巡遠村塢，令其招降鄉曲。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yong'an era he was captured by Xiao Yan's general Wei Xiu and others, bound facing the blade; they toured distant villages and stockades, ordering him to summon his neighbors to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yong'an era he was captured by Liang general Wei Xiu. Bound and facing execution, he was marched through distant hamlets and ordered to urge his neighbors to surrender.

sentences.zh: 道登厲聲唱呼：「但當努力，賊無所能。

translations.literal: Daodeng shouted in a stern voice: "Only strive with all your might—the bandits can do nothing!"
translations.idiomatic: Daodeng shouted, "Stand firm—the enemy can do nothing against you!"

sentences.zh: 」賊遂屠戮之。

translations.literal: " The bandits thereupon slaughtered him.
translations.idiomatic: " The enemy then killed him.

sentences.zh: 又荊州被圍，行臺宗靈恩遣使宗女等四人入城曉喻，為賊將所獲，執女等巡城，令其改辭。

translations.literal: Moreover, when Jing Province was besieged, Mobile Headquarters Zong Ling'en sent envoys Zong Nü and four others into the city to instruct and persuade; they were seized by a bandit general, who led the women around the wall and ordered them to change their words.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing Province was besieged, field headquarters chief Zong Ling'en sent four envoys including Zong Nü into the city to rally the defenders. A rebel general captured them, paraded them along the wall, and ordered them to change their message.

sentences.zh: 女等大言：「天軍垂至，堅守莫降。

translations.literal: The women spoke loudly: "The heavenly army is about to arrive—hold firm and do not surrender!"
translations.idiomatic: The women cried out, "Imperial troops are near—hold fast and do not surrender!"

sentences.zh: 」賊忿，各刳其腹，然後斬首。

translations.literal: " The bandits in anger disemboweled each of them, then beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: " Enraged, the enemy disemboweled each of them and then cut off their heads.

sentences.zh: 二州表其節義，道登等並賜五品郡、五等子爵，聽子弟承襲。

translations.literal: The two provinces memorialized their integrity and righteousness; Daodeng and the others were all granted fifth-rank commandery titles and fifth-rank viscountcies, with permission for sons and younger brothers to inherit.
translations.idiomatic: Both provinces reported their fidelity. Daodeng and the others were granted fifth-rank commandery titles and viscountcies, heritable by their sons.

sentences.zh: 遣使詣所在弔祭。

translations.literal: Envoys were dispatched to their locales to offer condolences and sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent envoys to their home districts to perform mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 李几，博陵安平人也。

translations.literal: Li Ji was a man of Anping in Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji came from Anping in Boling.

sentences.zh: 七世共居同財，家有二十二房，一百九十八口，長幼濟濟，風禮著聞，至於作役，卑幼競進。

translations.literal: Seven generations dwelt together sharing property; the household had twenty-two branches and one hundred ninety-eight mouths; young and old were numerous in orderly array, their customs and rites renowned; when it came to labor, the younger vied to press forward.
translations.idiomatic: Seven generations lived together under one roof with shared property—twenty-two branches and 198 mouths. Young and old alike were orderly and renowned for their propriety; even the youngest hurried to take up any task.

sentences.zh: 鄉里嗟美，標其門閭。

translations.literal: The district sighed in admiration and posted a plaque at their gate and lane.
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors marveled at their household, and the court ordered a commemorative plaque at their gate.

sentences.zh: 張安祖，河陽人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Anzu was a man of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Anzu came from Heyang.

sentences.zh: 襲世爵山北侯。

translations.literal: He inherited the hereditary enfeoffment as Marquis of Shanbei.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the hereditary title Marquis of Shanbei.

sentences.zh: 時有元承貴，曾為河陽令，家貧，且赴尚書求選，逢天寒甚，遂凍死路側。

translations.literal: At the time there was Yuan Chenggui, who had once been magistrate of Heyang; his family was poor, and as he was going to the Ministry of Personnel to seek appointment, he encountered severe cold and froze to death by the roadside.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yuan Chenggui, a former magistrate of Heyang, was traveling to the Ministry of Personnel to seek an appointment. The weather turned bitterly cold and he froze to death by the road.

sentences.zh: 一子年幼，停屍門巷，棺斂無託。

translations.literal: He left a young son; the corpse lay in the lane before the gate with no one to arrange the coffin and burial.
translations.idiomatic: He left a young son; the body lay in the street with no one to bury it.

sentences.zh: 安祖悲哭盡禮，買木為棺，手自營作，斂殯周給。

translations.literal: Anzu wept in full mourning rites, bought wood for a coffin, worked on it with his own hands, laid out the body, and provided fully for the burial.
translations.idiomatic: Anzu mourned him with full rites, bought wood and built the coffin with his own hands, and saw to the entire funeral.

sentences.zh: 朝野嘉歎。

translations.literal: Court and commoners alike praised and sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Court and country alike praised his conduct.

sentences.zh: 尚書聞奏，標其門閭。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel heard and memorialized; a plaque was posted at his gate and lane.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry reported his deed, and the court ordered a plaque at his gate.

sentences.zh: 王閭，北海密人也。

translations.literal: Wang Lü was a man of Mi in Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lü came from Mi in Beihai.

sentences.zh: 數世同居，有百口。

translations.literal: Several generations dwelt together, numbering a hundred mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Several generations lived together under one roof, a household of a hundred mouths.

sentences.zh: 又太山劉業興四世同居，魯郡蓋儁六世同居，並共財產，家門雍睦。

translations.literal: Moreover Liu Yexing of Mount Tai dwelt together four generations, and Gai Jun of Lu Commandery six generations—all sharing property, their households harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yexing of Mount Tai lived together four generations, and Gai Jun of Lu Commandery six—all sharing property in harmonious households.

sentences.zh: 鄉里敬異。

translations.literal: Their districts revered and marveled at them.
translations.idiomatic: Their neighbors held them in awe and respect.

sentences.zh: 有司申奏，皆標門閭。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized, and plaques were posted at all their gates and lanes.
translations.idiomatic: Officials reported their conduct, and commemorative plaques were posted at all their gates.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：于什門等或臨危不撓，視死如歸；

translations.literal: The historiographer states: Yu Shenmen and others, some facing peril without yielding, viewing death as returning home;
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Men such as Yu Shenmen faced danger without flinching and met death as if going home;

sentences.zh: 或赴險如夷，惟義所在。

translations.literal: some going into danger as if onto level ground, wherever righteousness lay.
translations.idiomatic: others entered peril as calmly as level ground, wherever duty called.

sentences.zh: 其大則光國隆家，其小則損己利物。

translations.literal: In the great case they glorified the state and elevated the clan; in the small they harmed themselves to benefit things and others.
translations.idiomatic: At their grandest they brought honor to state and clan; at their humblest they sacrificed themselves for others.

sentences.zh: 故其盛烈所著，與河海而爭流；

translations.literal: thus the splendor they achieved vies in flow with rivers and seas;
translations.idiomatic: Their renown races the rivers and seas in its reach;

sentences.zh: 峻節所標，共松栢而俱茂。

translations.literal: the stern integrity they marked flourishes together with pine and cypress.
translations.idiomatic: the integrity they embodied endures with pine and cypress.

sentences.zh: 並蹈履之所致，身歿名立，豈徒然哉。

translations.literal: All were brought about by treading and practicing it; the body perishes but the name is established—how could it be in vain?
translations.idiomatic: All this came of living what they preached: bodies may perish, but names endure. Their deaths were not in vain.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation Notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation Notes

sentences.zh: 魏書卷八十七 諸本目錄此卷注「闕」，卷末附宋人校語

translations.literal: In the table of contents of various editions of Wei Shu, juan 87 is marked "deficient"; at the end of the juan is appended Song-dynasty collation commentary
translations.idiomatic: Various editions of the Wei Shu mark juan 87 as deficient in their tables of contents; Song-dynasty collation notes are appended at the end of the scroll.

sentences.zh: 〈殿本入考證〉

translations.literal: 〈Entered into Textual Verification in the Palace Edition〉
translations.idiomatic: (Palace Edition, Textual Verification)

sentences.zh: 云：「魏收書節義傳亡。

translations.literal: stating: "Wei Shou's original 'Biographies of Integrity and Righteousness' is lost."
translations.idiomatic: which states: "Wei Shou's original chapter on righteous fidelity is lost."

sentences.zh: 」按傳序與北史卷八五節義傳序不同，當自原序刪節。

translations.literal: " According to this, the preface to the biographies differs from the preface to the 'Integrity and Righteousness' biographies in Beishi juan 85; it must have been abridged from the original preface.
translations.idiomatic: " The chapter preface differs from that in Beishi juan 85 and was evidently abridged from the original.

sentences.zh: 諸傳中只于什門傳稍詳於北史，王玄威傳所載詔書有溢出北史所載的文句，其他諸傳偶有一二字溢出，大抵全同北史。

translations.literal: Among the biographies only the biography of Yu Shenmen is somewhat fuller than in Beishi; the edict recorded in Wang Xuanwei's biography has passages exceeding what Beishi records, while the other biographies occasionally have a character or two in excess—on the whole they are entirely the same as Beishi.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yu Shenmen's biography is somewhat fuller than in the Beishi; Wang Xuanwei's biography preserves edict language not found there; other biographies differ by a word or two at most—overall the text matches the Beishi nearly completely.

sentences.zh: 諸人事迹本無可述，原文也必甚簡略。

translations.literal: The deeds of these men in themselves had little to relate; the original text must also have been very brief.
translations.idiomatic: These figures had little to recount in any case; the original text was surely very brief.

sentences.zh: 此卷多數傳文全同北史，或由於所據的史鈔和北史都是直錄魏書，非必以北史補。

translations.literal: Most of the biographical texts in this juan are entirely the same as Beishi—perhaps because the historical excerpts on which both drew directly copied the Wei Shu, and it is not necessarily that Beishi was used to supplement.
translations.idiomatic: Most of this juan matches the Beishi verbatim, perhaps because both drew on excerpts copied directly from the Wei Shu—not necessarily because the Beishi was used to fill gaps.

sentences.zh: 大義重於至聞自日人 殿本考證云：「首九字訛舛，不可推尋。」

translations.literal: "Great righteousness outweighs the utmost renown-since-ancient-days-among-people"—Palace Edition Textual Verification states: "The first nine characters are corrupt and cannot be reconstructed."
translations.idiomatic: On the corrupt opening line "大義重於至聞自日人": the Palace Edition notes that the first nine characters are damaged beyond recovery.

sentences.zh: 歷二十四年 通鑑卷一二二

translations.literal: On "after twenty-four years"—Zizhi Tongjian juan 122
translations.idiomatic: On "twenty-four years": Zizhi Tongjian, juan 122

sentences.zh: 〈三八五三頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 3853〉

sentences.zh: 記于什門還魏於元嘉十一年

translations.literal: records Yu Shenmen's return to Wei in the eleventh year of Yuanjia
translations.idiomatic: records Yu Shenmen's return to Wei in Yuanjia 11

sentences.zh: 〈魏延和三年

translations.literal: 〈Northern Wei Yanhe year 3
translations.idiomatic: (Northern Wei Yanhe 3

sentences.zh: (四三四)〉
，「二十四」作「二十一」。

translations.literal: , with "twenty-four" written as "twenty-one."
translations.idiomatic: , reading "twenty-one" instead of "twenty-four."

sentences.zh: 考異云：「後魏本紀

translations.literal: Examination of Discrepancies states: "The Later Wei Basic Annals
translations.idiomatic: Examination of Discrepancies notes: "The Later Wei annals

sentences.zh: 〈卷三〉

translations.literal: 〈juan 3〉
translations.idiomatic: (juan 3)

sentences.zh: 神瑞元年

translations.literal: Shenrui year 1
translations.idiomatic: Shenrui 1

sentences.zh: 〈四一四〉
八月遣于什門招諭馮跋，至此年二十一年矣。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Yu Shenmen was sent to summon and instruct Feng Ba; by this year twenty-one years had passed.
translations.idiomatic: sent Yu Shenmen in the eighth month to negotiate with Feng Ba—twenty-one years by this date.

sentences.zh: 若二十四年，乃在太延三年，而太延二年馮氏亡矣。

translations.literal: If it were twenty-four years, that would fall in Taiyan year 3, yet the Feng clan perished in Taiyan year 2.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-four years would place the return in Taiyan 3, but the Feng state fell in Taiyan 2.

sentences.zh: 」按傳稱「馮文通上表稱臣，乃送什門歸」，卷四上世祖紀上延和三年三月記「文通遣尚書高顒上表稱藩」，故通鑑置於是年。

translations.literal: " According to the biography, "Feng Wentong submitted a memorial declaring himself a subject, and only then was Shenmen sent back"; juan 4A, Basic Annals of Emperor Shizu, Yanhe year 3 third month records "Wentong sent the Minister of Works Gao Yan to submit a memorial declaring himself a vassal"—hence the Zizhi Tongjian places it in that year.
translations.idiomatic: " The biography says Feng Wentong submitted and Shenmen was released; the annals for Yanhe 3, month 3 record Feng Wentong's submission—hence the Tongjian dates the return to that year.

sentences.zh: 疑「二十四」當作「二十一」。

translations.literal: It is suspected that "twenty-four" should read "twenty-one."
translations.idiomatic: "Twenty-four" is probably a corruption for "twenty-one."

sentences.zh: 河中蒲坂人也 北史卷八五石文德傳「河中蒲坂」作「中山蒲陰」。

translations.literal: "A man of Puban in Hedong"—in Beishi juan 85, biography of Shi Wende, "Puban in Hedong" is written as "Puyin in Zhongshan."
translations.idiomatic: On "Puban in Hedong": Beishi juan 85 reads "Puyin in Zhongshan" instead.

sentences.zh: 按蒲坂自來屬河東郡，魏也無「河中」郡名。

translations.literal: According to this, Puban has always belonged to Hedong Commandery, and Wei also has no commandery named "Hedong Central."
translations.idiomatic: Puban belonged to Hedong Commandery; Northern Wei had no "Hedong Central" commandery.

sentences.zh: 卷一０六上地形志上定州北平郡有蒲陰縣，北平郡乃孝昌二年分中山置。

translations.literal: Juan 106A, Treatise on Geography, states that Ding Province, Beiping Commandery has Puyin County; Beiping Commandery was split from Zhongshan in Xiaochang year 2.
translations.idiomatic: Geography juan 106A lists Puyin County in Beiping Commandery, Ding Province; Beiping was carved from Zhongshan in Xiaochang 2.

sentences.zh: 若非「中」為「東」字之訛，則「河中蒲坂」為「中山蒲陰」之訛。

translations.literal: If "central" is not a corruption for "east," then "Puban in Hedong Central" is a corruption for "Puyin in Zhongshan."
translations.idiomatic: Unless zhong (central) is a corruption of dong (east), "Puban in Hedong" should read "Puyin in Zhongshan."

sentences.zh: 縣令范道榮先自朐城歸款以除縣令 諸本「朐」作「眴」，北史卷八五邵洪哲傳作「眗」。

translations.literal: "The magistrate Fan Daorong earlier submitted from Qucheng in allegiance to be removed as magistrate"—in various editions "Qucheng" is written as "Xuan"; Beishi juan 85, biography of Shao Hongzhe, writes "Ju."
translations.idiomatic: On "submitted from Qucheng": other editions read xuan or ju; Beishi juan 85 agrees the place name is Qucheng.

sentences.zh: 冊府卷一三八

translations.literal: Cefu juan 138
translations.idiomatic: Cefu yuan gui, juan 138

sentences.zh: 〈一六六六頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 1666〉

sentences.zh: 、卷八０三

translations.literal: , juan 803
translations.idiomatic: and juan 803

sentences.zh: 〈九五四八頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 9548〉

sentences.zh: 並作「朐」。

translations.literal: Both read "Qucheng."
translations.idiomatic: Both passages read "Qucheng."

sentences.zh: 按「朐城歸款」事見卷八世宗紀永平四年四月、卷四七盧淵附盧昶傳、卷九八蕭衍傳，「朐城」亦作「朐山」。

translations.literal: According to this, the matter of "Qucheng submitting in allegiance" appears in juan 8, Basic Annals of Emperor Shizong, Yongping year 4 fourth month; juan 47, biography of Lu Chao appended to Lu Yuan; and juan 98, biography of Xiao Yan—and "Qucheng" is also written as "Qushan."
translations.idiomatic: The "Qucheng submission" is recorded in the annals for Yongping 4, month 4, in the biography of Lu Chao (appended to Lu Yuan), and in the biography of Xiao Yan; the place is also called Qushan.

sentences.zh: 「眴」「眗」都是「朐」之訛，今據改。

translations.literal: "Xuan" and "Ju" are both corruptions of "Qu"; the text is now emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: The variants xuan and ju are both corruptions of qu; the text is emended to Qucheng accordingly.
